measurement_revisions.initial_matrices: Bounded pool with 3*C per live job. The final additional retired-batch reserve does not change stage code; final full run rechecks the 128-sample window with that reserve.
measurement_revisions.final_memory_guard: 3*C scratch per outstanding job plus 3*largest*(worker_count-1) retired-batch reserve. Automatic/interval capacity reserves both.

initial_failures: Sandbox import/logging could not create local sockets or user logs; native reruns used approved host execution.
First pool import/session attempt failed GDScript bool type inference; corrected before subsequent native validation.
First race run had four failed shrink assertions because the test cap was smaller than one full sample; cap corrected, 1800 checks passed.
First complete four-worker run recorded 2043396096 bytes process swap; live-only reservation was not accepted as memory validation. Added retired-batch reserve and reran.
limits: Measurements are one Linux desktop and one unchanged production capture; no broad CPU/RAM/OS/cgroup validation.
CPU per-core counters are system-wide; no hardware bandwidth/allocator-lock attribution.
RSS includes allocator/engine/driver pages; exact per-buffer transient peak is not isolated. Explicit reservation and process high-water marks are reported separately.
OS file cache and desktop activity were uncontrolled. Initial memory state differs between long runs; this is not proof that a reserve prevents swapping under arbitrary external pressure.
2x/4x require 20/40 samples per second and remain below target; field waits persist.
Whole-file strict payload verification was not repeated on the 125.95 GB production file. Selected production byte oracles and every synthetic fixture sample/channel are checked.
Rendering/presentation tail latency remains; no universal uninterrupted rendering or fixed-frame-rate claim.
Full production playback on Compatibility and cross-platform thread/memory behavior are not measured.
